title: Dynamic Canary Composer with statistical step advancement & shadow mirroring
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a Dynamic Canary Composer service and accompanying policy DSL that automates multi-step canary rollouts across model variants. The composer will support: weighted traffic schedules, statistical step advancement (significance testing + Bayesian bandit fallback), shadow traffic mirroring, automated rollback/circuit-breakers, and a simulation mode for preflight validation. Integrate telemetry hooks into Redwood Console for per-step SLO/quality signals (latency, error rate, token-level regressions, hallucination rate). The goal is to let Product/Platform teams declare rollout intents and safety constraints rather than write ad-hoc scripts.
acceptance_criteria: Composer accepts a declarative policy and materializes a step schedule with weights and time windows
Step advancement uses configurable tests (e.g., t-test, sequential probability ratio test) and respects minimum sample counts
Shadow mirroring can be enabled per-route with sampling ratio and option to drop responses from mirrored calls to avoid side effects
Automatic rollback triggers when any configured metric breaches thresholds for the configured duration
Simulation mode can run a candidate policy against historical request traces and produce a report showing expected traffic and guardrail hits
Events emitted to Console include step transitions, policy-evaluation reasons, and rollback justification with links to supporting metrics
tasks: Design policy DSL grammar and YAML schema (supports: steps, metrics, tests, bandit config, mirror rules, fallback model list)
Implement composer service that compiles policy -> runtime schedule and exposes a REST API
Implement statistical engine: sequential tests + configurable alpha/beta + min-samples
Add Canary Simulator that replays stored traces with policy logic and produces a dry-run report
Wire telemetry: emit per-step events to Console and create dashboard templates
E2E tests: integration with router to apply weight updates and validate mirror traffic behavior
Security review & RBAC for who can create/approve policies
decision_log: 2026-02-12: Chose sequential probability ratio test (SPRT) as default for fast step decisions; make test pluggable to allow t-test or nonparametric tests
2026-02-18: Add Bayesian multi-armed bandit fallback when significance is inconclusive after configured max-duration
2026-02-25: Mirror traffic will be non-blocking by default; mirrored responses are not surfaced to callers to avoid side effects
2026-03-02: Minimum sample thresholds enforced per-step to avoid early promotion on small traffic spikes
comments: 2026-02-10 Aisha Patel: Filed initial spec and prototype DSL sketch in docs/rollouts/dynamic-composer.md (see link)
2026-02-16 Marcus Chen: Implemented prototype REST skeleton and basic step materialization; demoed to PMs — feedback: need explicit rollback reason codes
2026-02-22 Lucia Gómez (PM): Requested inclusion of hallucination-quality metric (automated evals) as a first-class signal
2026-03-04 SRE review: Raised concern about rapid weight churn causing router instability; added rate limit on weight updates and backpressure window
2026-03-10 Design review: UX should show simulated user impact per-step (QPS, expected latency change) in Console rollout flyout
notes: Policy DSL example (YAML) included in spec page; minimal example: 'steps: - duration: 30m weight: 10% metrics: - name: latency.p95 op: lt threshold: 250ms test: sprt min_samples: 500'
Rollback reasons are codified: metric_breach | regression_detected | infra_failure | manual_abort; Console will display canonical reason and supporting metric snapshot
Mirroring considerations: add header X-Redwood-Mirror to preserve idempotency and to allow target models to ignore side effects
Simulator will provide a confidence band for metric estimates using bootstrap sampling over traces
implementation_plan: Phase 1: DSL + composer core + basic SPRT engine (sprint 1-2). Phase 2: simulator, mirror plumbing, Console events and dashboards (sprint 3). Phase 3: bandit fallback, RBAC + security review, runbook and pilot with two customer teams (sprint 4).
risks: Incorrect statistical configuration could lead to premature promotions — mitigate with conservative defaults and required approvals for P0 policies
Router instability from frequent weight updates — mitigate with update rate-limiting and batch apply windows
Telemetry gaps (missing labels or delayed metrics) could prevent automated step decisions — add fallback timeout and manual hold
